newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Profit-taking trims gain for Australia stocks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Profit-taking trims gain for Australia stocks.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2345 -2 US 30yr cl 6.84 -0.04
*Shares ended just firm, profit-taking eroding gains inspired by firm base metals and Dow. Volume 420.4 million shares worth A$1.04 bln, 1,015 stocks traded, 311 steady, 423 rises, 281 falls
Australian shares ended barely firmer on Thursday as profit-takers stepped in after the market touched a year high on early Dow-inspired gains.
The All Ordinaries index closed 0.3 points up at 2,314.9, after reaching an intra-day and year high of 2,341.3.
The September share price index closed two points down at 2,345 and at a 30.1 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said the market was bolstered early by a record high for the Dow and a modest recovery in base metal prices on Wednesday but investors began to take profits mid-morning.
"Profit-taking was fairly evident amongst the big banks whose gains have been the foundation for the local bourse's sustained rally," a dealer at a Sydney-based broker said.

The dealer said the big four banks, National Australia, Commonwealth, Westpac and ANZ, all saw early strong gains reversed after the midsession with Westpac stock the first to fall as investors decided to take profits.
"The pull-back was expected and may last another full session but I think the market has enough momentum to see it push through the (life-time high) 2,350 barrier early next week," the dealer said.

The retracement touched most sectors of the market with even the transport sector finishing only slightly firmer despite Wednesday's surprise bid for TNT by Dutch telcoms and postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN).

TNT stock itself slipped back slightly with dealers saying it appeared that KPN was not active in the issue after buying 9.9 percent of the company's ordinary and preferred stock on-market on Wednesday.
Emerging gold miner Ramsgate Resources topped turnover after its joint venture partner in the Mt Moner gold project, General Gold Resources, sold its 18-percent stake in Ramsgate on-market.

In other markets, Australian bonds held near new 2-1/2 year highs after another strong performance in the U.S. market. The yield on the 10-year T-bond finished at 7.63 percent, down 0.07 percentage points from Wednesday's closing level.
After showing early promise the Australian dollar finished weaker on the day due to profit-taking. At 5.05 p.m. (0705 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$7921/26.
